chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who works with the wealth on a basis of Mudarabah (profit-sharing), he said: The profit is for him, and there is nothing upon him from the loss, except if he differs in anything from what the owner of the wealth had instructed him.

key_terms.الْوَضِيعَة: The loss or diminution of capital.
key_terms.مُضَارَبَة: Mudarabah, a profit-sharing partnership where one party provides capital and the other provides labor.

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for profit and loss in a Mudarabah partnership according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the risk allocation in *Mudarabah*, establishing that the worker (*‘amil*) retains the profit while bearing no loss unless he commits *khilaf* (deviation) from the capital owner’s specific directives. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that financial liability in partnership is conditional upon adherence to agreed-upon terms, distinguishing between mere business risk and fault-based liability.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Nu’man, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding the man who works with the wealth on a ‘مُضَارَبَةً’ speculative profit-sharing basis. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For him would be the profit and there would be nothing upon him from the losses except if he were to oppose from anything from what he had been instructed with by the owner of the wealth’.
en.sarwar: 7. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has said the following: “About the case of a man who works for Mudarabah (profit sharing), abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, has said, ‘He can have (his share of) the profit but is not liable for depreciation (loss) unless he violates the instructions of the owner of the assets.”’
